title: Lakestone Logistics - Renewal + Scale / EU region onboarding check-in
next_steps: Redwood to send revised capacity + pricing quote for 2x reserved GPUs by 2027-01-05
Schedule technical trial kickoff for EU private deployment week of 2027-01-09
Customer to share current throughput traces and top 20 prompts (anonymized) by 2026-12-27
Security team to review SOC 2 / ISO artifacts shared link
action_items: Alice Chen: Draft and send updated quote for 2x reserved capacity - due 2027-01-05
Marcus Li: Prepare pilot runbook and EU private deployment checklist - due 2027-01-07
Samir Das (Lakestone): Export and share production token traces & prompt set - due 2026-12-27
Nora Kim (Lakestone): Provide KMS / key management requirements and any network constraints - due 2026-12-29
Priya Raman: Book follow-up meeting (30 min) for 2027-01-12 - due 2026-12-21
summary: Renewal and expansion check-in focused on Lakestone's intent to double reserved capacity, onboard EU private region, and extend contract term. Action items: Redwood to provide revised quote and pilot plan; customer to share traces and security requirements. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, fallback routing to hosted endpoints during pilot, and procurement timeline (end of January target).
transcript:
00:00 Raj Patel: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I think we got the main people on from Lakestone.
00:10 Alice Chen (Redwood AE): Hi Raj, hey team — Alice from Redwood. Quick intros?
00:15 Sofia Garcia: Sofia here, Head of ML, focusing on model infra and quality.
:20 Marcus Li (Redwood SE): Marcus, SE — I'll be running the pilot with you and looking at latency profiles.
00:25 Tom Reed (Lakestone, Procurement): Tom in procurement, I'll be managing the contract timing.
00:31 Nora Kim (Lakestone, Security): Nora, security — will review SOC 2 / encryption and KMS stuff.
00:35 Alice Chen: Cool. Goal for today is to align on the capacity bump, EU private onboarding, and next steps for the renewal. Roughly 30–45 minutes.
00:48 Raj Patel: For context, we've been on Dedicated with you for 9 months, and usage has grown 2.5x. We're seeing tail latency constraints during peak and want predictable throughput for our routing service.
01:05 Marcus Li: Got it. When you say tail latency, can you share the P95/P99 numbers? Even ballpark helps.
01:12 Raj Patel: P95 around 150ms, P99 up to 450ms during delivery windows — spikes when sequence length climbs for freight bookings.
01:25 Marcus Li: Okay that matches a batching/kv-cache behavior; where are you running today — single region us-east-1?
01:30 Samir Das: Yes, us-east only. We're pushing the EU launch in Q1 and want private tenancy there for GDPR/data residency.
01:40 Alice Chen: Perfect. So two asks: one is reserved capacity (looks like 2x more GPUs), and second is EU private deployment. We'll need to talk about provisioning lead time, SLAs and procurement cadence.
01:58 Raj Patel: Timeline — contract ideally in place by end of Jan, pilot in Jan, go-live EU mid Q1. Is that doable?
02:05 Marcus Li: On the technical side, yes. Provisioning for Dedicated or Private in EU usually has a 2–4 week lead once order is placed, depending on capacity. We can start a pilot earlier on hosted endpoints routed to EU region for validation, then flip to private.
02:24 Nora Kim: From security: what is the isolation model for Private? We need to know about KMS integration and audit logs. We also need SOC 2 artifacts, and if you support customer-managed keys (CMK).
02:38 Priya Raman (Redwood CSM): We have a private deployment option that supports customer KMS via our KMS connector and HSM integrations; we'll share the SOC 2 report and MOU for KMS.
02:50 Nora Kim: Cool — we'll want to see network/VPN topology too.
02:54 Marcus Li: Absolutely, we'll include the network diagram. Note: one thing to call out — when you're in private mode we still offer smart routing so during the pilot if capacity is exceeded we can automatically fallback to a hosted-compatible variant to keep requests flowing, with audit trail.
03:13 Sofia Garcia: Important for us — fallback behavior must preserve PII constraints; if it goes to hosted it needs to be redacted or have an opt-out.
03:25 Alice Chen: Understood. We can configure routing policies by customer and route non-sensitive workloads to hosted as a burst option. We'll note that for the pilot runbook.
03:36 Raj Patel: On pricing, can you share an estimate for 2x reserved capacity and a private region add-on? We need numbers for procurement.
03:45 Alice Chen: Yes — we'll send a revised quote. Ballpark today: the incremental reserved capacity is priced monthly; I'll prepare two options: one with 2x reserved GPUs with 12-month commit, and an option with a short-term 6-month ramp. We'll include cost for EU private infra and the setup fee.
04:05 Tom Reed: Procurement question — is there an early termination clause or credit if we overprovision?
04:12 Alice Chen: We have consumption credits and options for resize windows on a quarterly cadence; early termination terms are standard enterprise clauses — Marcus and I will flag the recommended terms to minimize risk.
04:25 Marcus Li: Technical thing — to hit your P99 target during peaks we'll recommend enabling prefix KV caching and aggressive batching thresholds for your most common prompt shapes. But that can increase token cost if not tuned.
04:40 Sofia Garcia: We're fine with a small cost uplift if it stabilizes tail latency. Can you share expected cost delta?
04:48 Marcus Li: We'll run a quick model with your traces — if you share top 20 prompts and token distribution, we can estimate token-per-request delta and suggested batching sizes.
05:00 Raj Patel: We'll export traces; Samir will take that.
05:06 Samir Das: Yep will do, anonymized traces by end of next week.
05:12 Nora Kim: A question about data retention — how long do you keep logs by default and can we set retention to 30 days?
05:19 Priya Raman: Default is 90 days for detailed logs, but we support configurable retention windows and can do 30 days for your account. We'll note that as part of the account config.
05:30 Raj Patel: What about encryption at rest — is that managed via our KMS?
05:33 Marcus Li: Yes, encryption at rest can be bound to your CMK in the private environment; hosted endpoints are encrypted with provider-managed keys unless you opt for CMK in Dedicated with KMS connector.
05:50 Tom Reed: Procurement timeline — we need an updated SOW with pricing and a draft contract by Jan 8 to review internally.
05:58 Alice Chen: We'll aim for that; action: Alice to send quote by Jan 5, Marcus to prepare SOW language for pilot by Jan 7.
06:08 Sofia Garcia: For pilot success criteria, here's what we care about: P95 under 200ms, P99 under 400ms for our freight prompts at 50% load; preserve response quality (no >5% hallucination increase), and ability to failover gracefully.
06:30 Marcus Li: We'll put those as measured success criteria in the pilot plan. We'll instrument synthetic load and also shadow your traffic for a week during pilot.
06:40 Raj Patel: Any blockers on EU data residency — what provenance do you need from us?
06:46 Marcus Li: Mainly network access, CIDR ranges, and compliance contact for audit artifacts. Also whether you require on-prem connectors vs VPC peering.
06:58 Samir Das: We prefer VPC peering to avoid VPN complexity.
07:02 Marcus Li: That's doable. We'll include peering steps in the runbook. There may be a short maintenance window for first sync of model layers in the EU region — usually under 1 hour.
07:15 Sofia Garcia: Regarding model variants — do we have to move to a smaller quantized variant to fit on our private infra? Concerned about quality loss.
07:24 Marcus Li: We support quantized variants and the runtime picks kernels to preserve quality. We'll include a quality regression check in the pilot and can fall back to a full precision variant if latency is unacceptable. We recommend starting with the same model you run in Dedicated and test quantized in parallel.
07:46 Nora Kim: Audit trail — does the console give per-token logs and immutable audit events? We need to show access logs to auditors.
07:55 Priya Raman: The Redwood Console includes per-route token-level cost breakdown and an audit log export; immutable events can be forwarded to your SIEM via our webhook. We'll provide a sample export.
08:10 Raj Patel: Ok, sounds good. Any competitor concerns? We've evaluated Anthropic and Bedrock — Bedrock had simpler marketplace billing but we prefer Redwood's batching and cost controls.
08:23 Alice Chen: Good to hear. We'll highlight the cost/perf tradeoffs in the quote.
08:28 Tom Reed: On contract length — is there a discount for 24 months vs 12?
08:33 Alice Chen: Yes, we'll show both 12- and 24-month pricing tiers in the quote, with higher discounts on 24-month commits.
08:40 Raj Patel: One last thing — can we get a shortcal on the legal/finance terms next week? Tom and I will be there.
08:46 Tom Reed: Yes available.
08:49 Alice Chen: Priya will set up a 30-min SOW/terms call; propose Jan 12 or Jan 13.
08:58 Priya Raman: I'll send invites after the call.
09:02 Marcus Li: Quick note on pilot instrumentation — we'll need a small feature flag to route a percentage of traffic to the pilot and sampling to compare outputs. That requires a deployment change on your side but minimal.
09:16 Samir Das: We can flip feature flags, that's fine. We'll coordinate with Marcus on the rollout plan.
09:25 Raj Patel: Great. Any other open questions?
09:30 Nora Kim: On KMS and CMK — will Redwood sign a key access attestation or do you provide a technical connector?
09:38 Marcus Li: There's a connector model; we provide a KMS sync pattern and limited key unwrap — we won't have access to raw keys. We'll provide the technical design for review.
09:52 Alice Chen: Ok team, quick recap of next steps: Redwood quote by Jan 5, pilot runbook by Jan 7, Lakestone to share traces by Dec 27, security docs shared by Redwood tonight. Priya to schedule follow-up Jan 12. Any objections?
10:12 Raj Patel: None, sounds good.
10:15 Alice Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links and the quote.
10:20 Meeting end.
